stem: Meera's teacher shows the class slides of different human cells under a microscope. One cell is very long and thin, with thread-like branches. Which statement best explains how this shape helps the cell perform its specific function?

options.text: The long, branched shape helps the nerve cell carry messages quickly over long distances in the body.
The long, branched shape helps the cheek cell form a flat protective lining inside the mouth.
The long, branched shape helps the muscle cell contract and relax to move body parts.
The long, branched shape helps the red blood cell carry more oxygen through its round disc shape.

teacher.key_rationale: A long, thin, branched structure is characteristic of a nerve cell (neuron); the length and branches allow impulses/messages to be carried over long distances and connected to many other cells. Options B, C, and D describe functions that belong to other cell types whose shapes differ (flat cheek cells, elongated fibres that contract, biconcave red blood cells), so only A correctly matches the described structure to its function.
